subject: Cognitive Science
title: Feature Integration Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Feature Integration Theory.

hook.text: Find the red circle among blue circles. Easy. Now find the red circle among red squares and blue circles.

buildup.text: The first search is instant—color pops out. The second takes time because you must bind two features.

discovery.text: Treisman's feature integration theory: single features are processed in parallel, but combinations need attention.

twist.text: Without attention, features float free. Patients with brain damage sometimes see 'illusory conjunctions'—wrong combos.

climax.text: Attention is the glue that binds color to shape to location into a unified object.

quiz.question: What does feature integration theory say attention does?

details.summary: Anne Treisman's feature integration theory explains how the brain binds separate visual features like color, shape, and orientation into unified objects. Pre-attentive processing detects features in parallel, but focused attention is needed to bind them together correctly.
details.whyItMatters: Feature integration theory explains visual search behavior and why we sometimes experience illusory conjunctions, seeing combinations of features that do not actually exist together.
takeaways: Basic features are processed in parallel across the visual field
Attention is required to bind features into complete objects
Without attention, features can be incorrectly combined

faq.question: What are illusory conjunctions?
faq.answer: Illusory conjunctions occur when features from different objects are incorrectly combined. For example, if a red circle and a blue square are briefly presented, you might report seeing a red square. This happens when attention is divided or overwhelmed.

faq.question: What is pre-attentive processing?
faq.answer: Pre-attentive processing detects basic features like color, orientation, and motion automatically and in parallel across the entire visual field. It is fast and effortless. A single red item among green items pops out pre-attentively without requiring focused serial search.
